title: Lambda versus EC2 and Fargate — when to choose
hook: Lambda excels at event-driven short tasks; EC2 and AWS Fargate fit long-running processes, WebSockets, and steady traffic where per-hour compute wins.

blocks.text: AWS Lambda charges per invoke and duration with 15-minute maximum timeout. Amazon EC2 provides virtual machines you manage — full OS control, any duration, WebSockets. AWS Fargate runs containers without managing EC2 — middle ground for always-on services. Decision factors: traffic pattern, connection model, duration, operational burden, and cost at steady state.

entries.plainDefinition: Serverless compute engine for ECS/EKS without managing EC2.
entries.example: Always-on API in container task 0.25 vCPU 512MB.

entries.plainDefinition: Lambda cannot run longer than 900 seconds.
entries.example: Long video transcode → Fargate or MediaConvert.

entries.plainDefinition: Persistent connection ill-suited to Lambda invoke model.
entries.example: API Gateway WebSocket with Lambda per message OK; not same as server-held socket on EC2.

entries.plainDefinition: Continuous load often cheaper on right-sized EC2/Fargate.
entries.example: 24/7 500 RPS API on c7g.large ASG vs Lambda bill.

blocks.text: Senior architects justify compute choice with traffic shape and ops cost. Wrong choice: WebSocket chat on Lambda (connection model mismatch) or cron every minute on EC2 t3.micro (Lambda cheaper).

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: Lambda event burst short; Fargate container steady; EC2 when need kernel, GPU, or lowest steady $ with RI.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Duration and model
items.body: Under 15 min event-driven → Lambda candidate. Hours → EC2/Fargate.

items.title: Traffic shape
items.body: Spiky/idle → Lambda. Flat 24/7 → EC2/Fargate with RI/Savings Plans.

items.title: Ops tolerance
items.body: Lambda least ops; EC2 most control; Fargate middle for containers.

snippet.label: Fargate task definition excerpt
snippet.code:
TaskDefinition:
  Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
  Properties:
    RequiresCompatibilities: [FARGATE]
    Cpu: "256"
    Memory: "512"
    NetworkMode: awsvpc
    ContainerDefinitions:
      - Name: api
        Image: !Sub "${AWS::AccountId}.dkr.ecr.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/api:latest"
        PortMappings:
          - ContainerPort: 8080
snippet.explanation: Fargate for always-on container without EC2 patching burden.

snippet.label: Lambda for S3 triggered ETL
snippet.code:
EtlFunction:
  Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
  Properties:
    Runtime: nodejs20.x
    Handler: index.handler
    Timeout: 300
    MemorySize: 1024
snippet.explanation: Short event-driven transform — Lambda sweet spot vs idle EC2.

snippet.label: ECS Fargate service create sketch
snippet.code:
aws ecs create-service \
  --cluster prod \
  --service-name api \
  --task-definition api:3 \
  --desired-count 2 \
  --launch-type FARGATE \
  --network-configuration "awsvpcConfiguration={subnets=[subnet-a,subnet-b],securityGroups=[sg-api],assignPublicIp=DISABLED}"
snippet.explanation: Multi-AZ Fargate behind ALB — parallel to EC2 ASG pattern.

blocks.title: Runtime and deployment parallels
rows: EC2 per second/hour; Fargate per task vCPU/GB hour

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Lambda for 24/7 high RPS API without cost model — EC2 may win. EC2 t3.micro for sporadic cron every hour — Lambda cheaper. Fargate for sub-second cron — Lambda simpler.

blocks.text: EKS on Fargate vs EC2 node groups trade ops vs cost. Lambda Function URLs for simple HTTP without API Gateway. How to prove it in production: Cost Explorer by service, P99 latency under load test, ops hours for patching EC2 AMIs.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Cold start P99; 29s API GW limit

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Lambda for everything or EC2 for everything gets rejected. Strong answer: traffic shape, duration, connection model, ops cost — hybrid common.

interviewTakeaways: Lambda: event-driven, short, spiky — not long TCP or >15 min jobs.
Fargate: containers without EC2 management for steady services.
EC2: full control, WebSockets, GPU, lowest steady cost with commitment.
60s: Burst short → Lambda. Steady container → Fargate. Kernel/long TCP → EC2. Calculate crossover.
Follow-up: when Step Functions over single Lambda?
commonPitfalls: WebSocket server entirely on Lambda — weak; API GW WebSocket per message differs from EC2 socket server.
Strong answer: persistent connections on EC2/Fargate; Lambda for handlers.
Ignoring Lambda 15-minute timeout for batch ETL.
EC2 for once-daily 30s cron — Lambda EventBridge schedule cheaper.
